relevance_note: Single case report of an adult with PFAPA syndrome carrying a heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant: 'We have found a novel mutation in the gene TNFAIP3 in an adult patient'.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; the JSON was assembled by a short Python script in which every span was cut programmatically from the paper text (to keep thin spaces, U+2010 hyphens and fullwidth % signs) and then checked verbatim. No tables in the paper. Labels: the single proband is 'patient'; tested relatives are 'his father', 'his sister' (both carriers, asymptomatic) and 'the patient's mother' (tested, no TNFAIP3 variant; no variants row). Variant printed four ways: 'c.63A>T (P.I21=)', 'c.63A>T(p. I21 = )', 'c.63 A>T(p. I21=)', 'c.63 A > T (p. I21 = )'; recorded from the Figure 1B legend. Variant type 'other' because the authors describe it as making no difference to amino acid composition (synonymous); authors classify it as VUS and diagnose PFAPA syndrome, not HA20. Inheritance recorded as paternal from the stated parental testing (father positive, mother negative) plus 'suggestion of heredity'. Contradictions: (1) red papules on the left thigh and a herpes zoster rash are reported in the case presentation, but the Discussion says 'no skin changes'; both rows emitted, checklist skin lesions set to not reported. (2) The case presentation describes fever for more than 1 year including an episode on April 30, 2021, before vaccination on June 4, 2021, while the Discussion says symptoms developed after COVID-19 vaccination. (3) 'hyperplastic bone marrow image' vs 'bone marrow examination showed no significant abnormalities'. (4) CRP printed as 'CRP7 0.30 mg/L' (likely garbled) while described elsewhere as slightly increased. Abstentions: 'no recurrent vulva ulcer' (male patient, verbatim) is narrower than genital ulcers and normal colonoscopy is narrower than GI inflammation, so both checklist items are not reported; normal chest CT not used to exclude interstitial lung disease; decreased monocyte % and T lymphocytes not counted as autoimmune cytopenia; headache not counted as CNS involvement; herpes zoster and COVID-19 not counted as recurrent infections; relatives' 'without any discomfort' recorded as one excluded feature each but not used to exclude any checklist item. Negative infection, tumor-marker, coagulation, culture and chromosome work-up results were not entered as phenotypic features. Age 25 taken as age at last evaluation/report; age at diagnosis not stated.
